## Summary

Concretum asks the regime question every intraday trend follower has: **can you tell in advance whether today is likely to be a trend day or a mean-reversion day?** Their candidate tell is **GEX** - dealers' aggregate gamma exposure, estimated from SPX open interest.

- **The mechanism (their primer):** dealers hedge their options books. **Long gamma** -> they buy dips and sell rallies to stay delta-hedged, which leans against moves (dampens volatility, mean-reversion-friendly). **Short gamma** -> they sell into weakness and buy into strength, reinforcing moves (trend-friendly).
- **The assumption under attack:** the classic open-interest GEX (they cite SqueezeMetrics' GEX methodology and SpotGamma's Market Gamma model) cannot see which side dealers are on, so it assumes **dealers are long calls and short puts**. Their words: "a strong and fragile assumption"; "a proliferation of online providers selling GEX estimates based on a flawed assumption".
- **How the GEX number is built (formulas are images in the post; reconstructed from the surrounding text):** dollar gamma per contract = side x M x gamma x 0.01 x S^2 (side +1 long / -1 short, M = multiplier, S = underlying price; "dollars of delta exposure per 1% move"); GEX = the open-interest-weighted sum of that across strikes and expiries, puts entering with a minus sign. Their toy chain (two strikes x three expiries, invented inputs): calls +$65,000, puts -$91,000, aggregate GEX **-$26,000** - dealers short gamma overall under the assumed positions.
- **Study design (from the free half):** almost 15 years of SPX options data; GEX computed for **same-day, 1-30-day and >30-day expiries, plus the aggregate**. Two questions: (1) is an intraday price move more likely to continue over the **next 30 minutes** when GEX is negative rather than positive? (2) does an intraday trend-following strategy improve by **trading only when GEX < 0**? Strategy returns are measured **before trading costs**.
- **Chart (tweet, cumulative view):** "GEX and next-30-minute SPY momentum". Y = cumulative timing return (percentage points), ticks 0-80; X = Net GEX (USD bln / 1% move; percentile spacing), ticks -30, -15, -5 | GEX = 0 | 2, 8, 14, 22, 32, 49 bln. Observations sorted by GEX and split at the divider into a negative-GEX half (red line) and a positive-GEX half (green line), each with a dashed straight mean line. **Negative-GEX half: climbs from 0 to a peak of about +66 pp just past -15 bln, dips, recovers to the low 60s near -5 bln, then slopes down to about +45 pp at the divider; annotated mean +0.31 bps per observation. Positive-GEX half: flat-to-down from about +45 pp to about +34 pp (low near +27 pp around +32 bln); annotated mean -0.05 bps per observation.**
- **What the numbers say:** the sign flips exactly as the gamma story predicts - negative GEX (dealers short gamma) comes with slight continuation, positive GEX with a slight fade. The magnitude is tiny: +0.31 bps per 30-minute bar **before costs**. And it is not monotonic in GEX: the line is steepest around -15 bln and slopes *down* into the divider, i.e. bars with small negative GEX showed slightly negative continuation.
- **Not captured (paywalled):** the strategy-level answer to question 2 (trend-following with vs without the GEX < 0 filter, per expiry bucket), sample sizes, significance testing, and any GEX construction detail beyond the primer.

## Why it matters

- **A cheap regime test for the vault's intraday-trend cluster.** [[2026-11-22-algojan-noise-band-intraday-momentum-mnq]], [[2026-11-19-algojan-vwap-pullback-topstep-mnq]] and [[2026-11-11-propquantx-nq-gap-up-breakout]] are all continuation bets whose edge should, on this theory, concentrate on negative-GEX days. A GEX-sign split is a one-column group-by on their trade logs - worth adding to each replication checklist, *if* the effect shows up in NQ/MNQ and after costs.
- **A skeptic's test of a popular paid signal, from a shop with no GEX product to protect.** Same evidentiary shape as [[2026-10-18-concretum-chasing-skew-trend-following]]: take a marketed property, measure it observation by observation. The primer is also the cleanest walkthrough of delta/gamma hedging and the GEX formula in the vault so far.
- **Same shop, consistent programme:** after flows ([[2026-09-18-concretum-rebalancing-flows-alpha]]), skew ([[2026-10-18-concretum-chasing-skew-trend-following]]) and Clenow-style trend ([[2026-10-24-concretum-clenow-trend-model-etfs]]), this is their intraday-regime line (their 2026 archive also lists intraday seasonality of trends, a 0DTE overlay, leveraged-ETF flows and a session-dependence study - none captured yet).
- **Mirror reading for mean-reversion is weak:** GEX > 0 averages -0.05 bps - closer to "no continuation" than "strong reversal". It does not by itself flag a mean-reversion day for the MR notes ([[2026-11-05-systematicpeter-intraday-russell-mean-reversion]]).
- **Skepticism gates:** (1) cumulative charts flatter small edges - the eye sees a line at +45 pp, the mean is +0.31 bps; (2) **before costs**, by the authors' own statement; (3) SPX GEX is an SPX/SPY dealer-book signal - an NQ/MNQ strategy trades a different book; (4) only three of the nine GEX tick labels are negative and the negative region spans roughly a third of the chart width, so negative-GEX looks like the minority regime - the left half rests on fewer observations; (5) the article's own framing says open-interest GEX may not measure dealer positioning at all - the sign result is only as good as that proxy; (6) strategy-level results and significance unverified (paywalled); (7) chart levels are approximate readings (+/-1-2 pp) - the two means are exact annotation text.
- **Isolation note (CoS convention):** personal second-brain knowledge capture only; nothing routed to the trading company.
